- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce peak overshoots by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.50) and forecast is still trending up, apply downward bias correction, especially in the first 5–7 days of the forecast horizon.
- For long-term forecasts (e.g., 30-day), if recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of declining prices), reduce forecasted highs and increase lows by 3–5%.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00–0.33), avoid large swings; use smoother, trend-following adjustments rather than sharp directional moves.
- If forecast shows a spike followed by a sharp drop (e.g., 2–3 consecutive days of high then low), apply a “lag correction” — reduce the peak by 5–10% and shift the trough slightly earlier.
- For forecasts with high sentiment volatility, use a “sentiment-weighted smoothing” — overweight recent sentiment in the last 3–5 days when adjusting for next-day price direction.
